provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation:
Mechanism: the foreground blob (palette[5]) must be exactly covered by 2x2 squares and straight 3-cell bars. Squares are painted palette[8], bars palette[2], and the background palette[0] is left unchanged.

The emitted program works in visible coordinates. It takes the first uncovered blob cell in visible reading order. Every cell before it is already covered, so that cell must be the top-left of a square, the left end of a horizontal bar, or the top of a vertical bar. The program tries each, recurses, and backtracks on failure.

The set {square, horizontal bar, vertical bar} maps onto itself under all eight D4 transforms. The exact-cover condition is therefore the same rule in any visible orientation, and no direction constants are needed.

The earlier factory's square-count prior has been removed. It was 2 or 3 squares depending on the generator-width axis, which is a generator-correlated heuristic and does not resolve ambiguity.

The constructor repair keeps the original sampling logic, ranges, object counts and explicit fixtures. It adds a rejection filter that enumerates every square/bar exact cover of the sampled blob and keeps the scene only if all covers give the same colouring. This makes the label a function of the visible input, independent of any solver's search order.

By hand I traced all four canonical fixtures (3 train, 1 test) and found exactly one tiling each, through forced bricks:
- train1: bar col3, square, then col6 bar and two squares.
- train2: square (1,2), bar col3, bar row2, bar row6, two squares.
- train3: bar row1, bar col3, two squares.
- test: bar row2, square, bar row0, bar col6, bar row4, two squares.
So the uniqueness filter agrees with the fixtures, and any exact-cover solver reproduces them under every D4 and palette. None of this has been executed.
draft_notes.limitations:
- Untested. Nothing here has been run; the host must execute both the constructor and the factory.
- Factory still fails against the unrepaired constructor. With the original constructor, ambiguous fresh scenes would still occur, and no input-only solver can be exact on them. The factory is only claimed correct together with the uniqueness-filtered sampler.
- Distribution shift. The filter changes the fresh-scene distribution: scenes whose blob has two or more distinct square/bar colourings are removed. Width 10-11 scenes have 3 boxes and up to 4 sticks and are probably rejected more often, which may slightly shift the width/height mix. Size ranges, brick counts, placement ranges and adjacency constraints are unchanged.
- Sampling bounds. Sampling is bounded at 2000 scene attempts × 20000 layout attempts per phase, and the generator raises RuntimeError if they are exhausted. The original inner loops were unbounded.
- Enumeration cap. Tiling enumeration is capped at 20000 covers; hitting the cap counts as ambiguous and the scene is rejected. Real blobs have at most 24 cells, so the cap should not bind.
- Fallback. If the foreground colour is absent, the program falls back to all non-background cells. If no exact cover exists (not possible for constructor scenes), the input is returned unchanged.
draft_notes.diagnosis:
The host counterexample (d4=0; palette 0->2, 5->6, 8->3, 2->8) fails on fresh train pair 1.

Forced bricks: the blob has a forced bar at (4,1-3), a forced square at (5,2)-(6,3) and a forced vertical bar at col 2 rows 1-3.

The remaining cells admit two exact covers with different colourings:
- Label: bar (1,3-5), square (2,3)-(3,4), square (1,6)-(2,7), bar (3,5-7).
- Reading-order backtracking result: square (1,3)-(2,4), bar (1,5-7), bar (3,3-5), square (2,6)-(3,7).

Both tilings have 3 squares and 4 bars, keep every anchor inside the generator's ranges, and pass its parallel-adjacency checks. The input therefore does not determine the output. The failure comes from label ambiguity in the constructor, not from a coordinate, D4 or palette error in the factory. The same reading-order failure would appear in the archived native solver.

Any tie-break, including the old square-count prior, a different scan order or a special case, would only move the failure to the mirrored scene. The justified repair is to reject ambiguous scenes at sampling time. The factory then just needs any exact cover.
draft_notes.constructor_issue:
The generator overlays independently sampled 2x2 boxes and 1x3/3x1 sticks into one grey blob. It records brick identity only in the output. Its anti-ambiguity checks only cover:
- boxes in the same row or column within 2 cells;
- same-orientation sticks in the same row or column within 1 cell.

These checks do not exclude blobs that have several exact square/bar tilings with different colourings, as in the host counterexample. Such labels depend on hidden latents (which bricks were sampled), so no solver that sees only inputs and demonstrations can be exact.

The proposed repair rejects random scenes unless every exact cover of the grey cells yields the same colouring. The check is order-independent enumeration, not a solver tie-break. The explicit fixture path, labels, size ranges and object counts are unchanged.

All canonical fixtures appear to have unique tilings (hand-traced, not executed), so no fixture contradiction was found. The repair requires host review and execution before application.
draft_notes.host_review: Explicit fixture inputs/outputs compared exactly to canonical source before applying. No smaller-object-count fallback allowed; exhaustion raises.
